messages:
Lisa (sales): Quick question — customer wants a 12-month reserved commit but traffic is very spiky (batch inference daytime, chat bursts evenings). They asked how many GPUs to reserve vs rely on autoscale/burst. Any rough calc we can give them for their SOW?

Marta (solutions): Do we have their traffic profile? avg qps and peak qps, plus avg tokens per request?

Lisa (sales): From their POE: avg 25 QPS daytime, peaks to ~220 QPS for 20-30s every few minutes. Median request ~120 tokens, worst-case 800 tokens. Latency SLO 250ms p95.

Raj (eng-infra): Rough back-of-envelope: assume model throughput ~1.2 tokens/ms per GPU at that seq len after quantization and batching. But heavy tail (800 tokens) will reduce effective QPS. We should size for steady-state + a burst buffer.

Sam (sre): Also depends on batching window. If we allow 20ms batching with continuous batching we can get much better utilization. For p95 250ms we can't batch too long. Recommend conservative 10ms batching for chat to meet SLO.

Marta (solutions): Here's a quick calc I used before:
```
- steady tokens/sec = avg_qps * avg_tokens = 25 * 120 = 3000 tps
- peak tokens/sec = peak_qps * avg_tokens = 220 * 120 = 26400 tps (but bursts include long requests)
- tokens per GPU (sustained) ~ 1.2 tokens/ms => 1200 tokens/sec
=> GPUs for steady = ceil(3000/1200) = 3
=> GPUs for peak (if sustained) = ceil(26400/1200) = 22
```
So reserved commit should cover steady + runway for autoscale safety margin (say x1.5) => recommend reserving 5 GPUs and rely on burst capacity/autoscale for spikes.

Lisa (sales): OK helpful. Customer worried about cost if spikes hit frequently. They asked if we have a "burst credit" model or pre-warmed pool that doesn’t cost as much as full reserved gpus.

Raj (eng-infra): We support burst capacity on Dedicated. Two knobs: 1) prewarm instances (idle but with warm caches) and 2) burst credits that let you exceed committed GPUs for short windows. Prewarm costs ~30% of a full GPU/hour but gives near-zero cold-start. Burst credits are consumed when autoscale goes above commit and refill slowly during low usage.

Marta (solutions): Proposal to customer: reserve 5 GPUs (predictable baseline), enable burst pool sized for +10 GPUs with burst-credit window 120s, and set autoscale to allow up to 20 GPUs if billing-approved. Add canary fallback to a smaller model when overload.

Raj (eng-infra): Example autoscale policy snippet we can share (high-level):
```
autoscale:
  target_utilization: 0.65
  min_replicas: 5
  max_replicas: 20
  scale_up_window: 30s
  scale_down_window: 120s
  burst_pool: 10 # transient, paid from burst credits
  prewarm: 2
```
Note: scale_up_window triggers more conservatively; for very short 20-30s bursts we want to rely on burst_pool + prewarm rather than scale-up.

Lisa (sales): Customer security question: if we add prewarm, are requests isolated to their VPC? They worry about other tenants seeing warm cache.

Sam (sre): Dedicated pools are single-tenant; prewarm is within their pool so KV caches are tenant-local. For Private (VPC) it's fully isolated, for Hosted Dedicated we still run in tenant-only GPUs. Add KMS for keying and we can include an audit note.

Marta (solutions): Also call out graceful degradation: set fallback route to a lighter quantized model (e.g., 8-bit distill) when GPUs > committed + burst. That reduces latency risk and cost.

Lisa (sales): I'll send them a short SOW blurb: reserve 5 GPUs, burst pool 10, autoscale to 20, prewarm 2, SLO 250ms p95 with fallback to quantized model when overload. Can someone review wording?

Raj (eng-infra): LGTM. Add line: "We recommend monitoring token distribution and periodic reevaluation (monthly) to adjust commit size."

Sam (sre): Also include cost note: if bursts exceed credits frequently we'll recommend moving to a larger commit or adjusting batching/quantization.

deploy-bot: [deploy] autoscale-policy-template v3 pushed to sales-snippets repo by Marta (solutions) :thumbsup:

Lisa (sales): Perfect — I'll loop in procurement and legal. Thanks team :rocket:
